title: Jake Castillo on scaling Cal AI to $40M ARR: UGC, influencers, paid ads, pricing and hiring
summary: Jake Castillo, Cal AI's CMO and COO, explains how Cal AI reached 15M users and $40M ARR in 18 months. He covers niching down, choosing between UGC, influencers and paid ads by cash position, running about 300 paywall tests, pricing, LTV, and hiring hungry people.

principles.text: Saturation isn't a barrier: win with a novel feature that removes friction, not a clone of incumbents.
principles.quote: if you have a product that has a novel feature and that feature is better than what's currently in the market, I I don't think you have to worry about saturation

principles.text: In a crowded category, niche down to a specific audience; niche drives the marketing angle, then the UI.
principles.quote: you start with the you start with the niche, then you go with the marketing angle, and then you can create your UI.

principles.text: UGC is a swing at the algorithm: pay flat fees, absorb risk upfront, and capture viral upside.
principles.quote: Pay flat fees. Absorb that risk upfront so you can capture the upside when it does eventually go viral.

principles.text: Vet creators by their comment section; real conversations signal real influence and can't be faked.
principles.quote: I you can't fake the comment section.

principles.text: Pick the channel by cash position: UGC if broke, influencers with some budget, paid ads once cash flow isn't a concern.
principles.quote: If like cash flow is not a concern, I think paid ads is a good place to play. If you are tight on money, I think UGC is the place to play

principles.text: LTV is what lets you outspend competitors on acquisition, so keep testing paywalls constantly.
principles.quote: It's the only way you will be able to durably win is if you can acquire customers at a higher cost than your competitors.
